SMTO-EXE-0085 — SMTO can't see a desktop on that computer

GUID: 305c263d-d58b-5cbd-ad59-24a4209c827d
Slug: screen-no-session
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: screen

What happened

  • SMTO tried to look at the screen of the computer it works on, but the Gateway there isn't running inside a signed-in desktop. Nothing was captured.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Go to the computer the Gateway runs on, sign in, and make sure its desktop is showing, not the login or lock screen. SMTO can only see a screen that belongs to a signed-in desktop.
  2. Start the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses on that computer) from inside that desktop, not from a remote terminal or as a background service. A Gateway started outside the desktop has no screen to look at, even when someone is signed in.
  3. If it was already started that way, run the Gateway installer again on that computer to repair it, without deleting the Gateway first. SMTO reports the same problem when the Gateway's screen parts failed to load.
  4. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Check connection for that Gateway, then start a New chat and ask again. Checking refreshes what the Gateway can do, and a new chat uses that updated list.

What success looks like

  • Asking SMTO to list the screens on that computer shows your displays instead of this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages that Gateway, saying which computer it is and how the Gateway is started. Don't point SMTO at a different computer's screen instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's screen adapter found no interactive desktop session (no DISPLAY on Linux, not on the macOS console, no accessible Windows input desktop, or the native screen module failed to load), so display observation is unavailable.

What this means

  • The screen adapter or readiness gate could not establish the interactive desktop session required for display observation. Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.

Why this can happen

  • The screen adapter or readiness gate could not establish the interactive desktop session required for display observation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect screen runtime readiness and the Gateway's logged-in session without requesting pixels as a discovery side effect.

How to fix it

  • Check the Gateway's screen readiness (unavailable_reason screen_no_session). Run the Gateway inside the logged-in user's interactive session: DISPLAY set on X11, on the console (CGSession) on macOS, an interactive input desktop rather than a service/session 0 on Windows. create_adapter also falls back to this state when the platform screen module fails to import, so confirm native screen dependencies are installed; then refresh the Gateway's capabilities and start a new task.
  • Log in to the selected Gateway desktop and start the Gateway in that session.

Retry and execution caution

  • Log in to the selected Gateway desktop and start the Gateway in that session.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended session reports display capability and returns its current display metadata.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass OS permissions, capture another Gateway, or copy screen content to diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
